City delays tram extension by a year

Works on the north line will now finish in 2027, with the council blaming a dispute over the depot site rather than the tunnelling itself.

Inês Kowalczyk Tue 11 Feb 2025 18.45 GMT

The tram extension that was to open next spring will not carry passengers until 2027, the council confirmed on Tuesday, after a year-long argument about where to put the depot that nobody involved had expected to still be running.

The tunnelling, which was the part everyone worried about, finished early and under budget. What stalled was the surface works at the northern end, where the original depot site turned out to belong to a trust whose consent the council had assumed rather than obtained.

We were wrong about which half of this project was hard, and we were wrong in public.

The transport committee's chair said the delay would not change the final cost, a claim the opposition disputed within the hour. Neither side produced a figure, and the published programme still carries the old opening date.

What happens to the buses

The replacement bus service on the northern corridor, which was to be withdrawn in April, will instead run for another two years. Drivers were told on Monday evening, before the announcement, which the union described as the only part of the process that had gone well.

Passengers on the corridor will see no change until 2027, and the council has promised a revised programme before the summer. What it does with the depot site is the question that decides what happens next.
